title: Customer-facing rolling upgrade playbook and zero-downtime migration utility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a reusable customer communications package and an accompanying lightweight migration utility to enable zero-downtime rolling upgrades across Hosted/Dedicated/Private customers. The package includes: an upgrade playbook with explicit rollout gates, a compatibility matrix for common API breaking surface areas, a compact changelog digest template, in-app/email snippets for staged notifications, and a small CLI tool (migration-scan) that helps customers detect and remediate likely compatibility issues before upgrade. Goal: reduce manual migration support and cut reactive rollback incidents by 50% for the next LTS->rolling transition.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published to Confluence and linked from public changelog page
Compatibility matrix covers: API fields, model behavior deltas, structured output, function/tool calling, and embeddings dimension changes
Migration-scan CLI prototype (node/python) can analyze a customer prompt set / SDK usage patterns and flag high-risk changes
Three email/in-app notification templates reviewed by Legal and Support and ready for staged send
Support runbook with rollback triggers and diagnosis checklist created and validated with SRE and Support in tabletop
content:
OVERVIEW:
This ticket creates a customer-facing playbook designed for rolling upgrades (LTS -> rolling, minor runtime bumps, and model pin migrations). We focus on zero-downtime approaches: compatibility detection, gradual traffic shifting, and clear customer comms so teams can plan safe upgrades without breaking production logic.

TARGET AUDIENCE:
- Platform and infra engineers at customers who run high-availability LLM endpoints
- Product/ML engineers who depend on deterministic outputs and embeddings
- Customer success and SRE teams inside Redwood who coordinate upgrades

PHASED ROLLOUT GATES (recommended):
1) Canary (internal + 2 pilot customers, <1% traffic) - verify latency and a curated prompt set
2) Expanded pilot (10% traffic, up to 5 customers in different regions) - run automated evals and compare quality metrics
3) Gradual ramp (10->50%) with monitoring thresholds for token error rate, latency p95, and quality regression alerts
4) Full switch when gate thresholds pass for 24h and no manual blockers

GATE METRICS & TRIGGERS:
- Latency p95: no more than 15% regression vs baseline
- Error rate: <0.2% increase in 1h rolling window
- Quality: auto-eval F1 / BLEU-like proxies show <2% regression on critical prompts
- Manual stop: any customer-reported functional regression or >10% traffic error spike

COMPATIBILITY MATRIX (example rows; customers get CSV export):
- API request field changes: none -> breaking if field dropped (mitigation: warn and keep alias fields for 2 major cycles)
- Structured output schema: earlier shape vs new keys (mitigation: schema version header + graceful fallback docs)
- Function calling signature changes: backward-compatible shim recommended
- Embedding dims: 1536 -> 2048 (breaking for downstream indexing; mitigation: reindex guide + dual-index period)
- Model tokenization differences affecting prompt length: document expected effective token delta and recommend prefix trimming rules

CHANGELOG DIGEST TEMPLATE (for customers):
- One-line summary: what changed and why it matters to customers
- Impact bullets: potential breaking surfaces and mitigations
- Upgrade guidance: quick steps and a link to the migration-scan tool
- Rollout plan: expected timelines, phases, and rollback path

MIGRATION- SCAN CLI (prototype usage):
- Purpose: scan customer prompt sets and SDK usage to identify high-risk upgrade items (embedding dimension assumptions, reliance on specific structured keys, function call signatures).
- Example: migration-scan analyze --project my-app --prompt-file prompts.json --output report.html
- Output sections: risk summary (high/medium/low), suggested quick fixes, links to docs and example PRs
- Distribution: single-file binary + pip/npm package depending on language preference; include docker image for air-gapped customers

EMAIL / IN-APP NOTIFICATION SNIPPETS (staged):
- Subject (pilot invite): "Action requested: opt-in pilot for Redwood runtime-1.20 rolling upgrade (low risk)"
- Body bullets: what we’re changing, why, pilot expectations, how to opt-in, link to migration-scan report and support contact
- Subject (general upgrade notice): "Planned upgrade: runtime-1.20 — staged rollout starts 2026-04-01"
- Banner (in-app): short line + link to migration scanner and docs (CTA: "Check compatibility")

ROLLBACK & SUPPORT PLAYBOOK (quick steps):
1) Detect: monitor rule fires for error/quality regression
2) Assess: run migration-scan against live requests and compare with pre-upgrade baseline
3) Contain: shift traffic back to previous model variant or capacity pool (automated traffic routing policy)
4) Root cause: capture request traces and failing prompt examples, open incident with engineering runbook
5) Communicate: send targeted customer acknowledgement and ETA for fix

DOCUMENTATION & ARTIFACTS TO DELIVER:
- Public changelog entry and private detailed migration guide (Confluence + PDF)
- CSV compatibility matrix and sample reindex playbook for embeddings changes
- migration-scan CLI binary + usage guide and Docker image for Private customers
- Email/in-app templates and a cutover checklist for customers and support

UNIQUE DECISIONS MADE (trade-offs):
- We will not enforce automatic schema translation for structured outputs in this cycle (too risky). Instead, provide schema-version header and conversion examples.
- migration-scan will be intentionally conservative: prioritize low false negatives, tolerate some false positives and actionable remediation guidance.

NEXT STEPS:
- Lock templates and run tabletop with Support & SRE (w/c 2026-03-15)
- Merge migration-scan prototype PR and publish Docker image to internal registry
- Schedule pilot invites and identify 2 low-risk pilot customers for canary
